title: Introduction to Programming
description: Foundational programming course covering variables, control flow, functions, lists, dictionaries, file input/output, and debugging in Python. Students complete weekly programming labs.

title: Data Structures
description: Arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, hash tables, heaps, and graphs. Emphasis on complexity analysis, recursive problem solving, and writing efficient implementations.

title: Discrete Mathematics
description: Propositional logic, proof techniques, sets, relations, functions, combinatorics, and elementary graph theory as preparation for upper-level computer science.

title: Computer Systems
description: Machine-level representation of programs, memory hierarchy, linking, processes, virtual memory, and concurrency. Includes weekly systems programming labs in C.

title: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
description: Divide-and-conquer, dynamic programming, greedy algorithms, graph algorithms, NP-completeness, and approximation. Students prove correctness and analyse running time.

title: Database Systems
description: Relational modelling, SQL, normal forms, indexing, transaction processing, and query optimisation. Semester project builds an application backed by a relational database.

title: Operating Systems
description: Processes and threads, CPU scheduling, synchronization, deadlock, memory management, file systems, and virtualisation. Includes a multi-week kernel-style project.

title: Computer Networks
description: Layered network architecture, packet switching, routing, reliable transport, congestion control, and application protocols. Labs use socket programming.

title: Artificial Intelligence
description: Search, constraint satisfaction, adversarial games, probabilistic reasoning, Markov decision processes, and an introduction to machine learning.

title: Machine Learning
description: Supervised and unsupervised learning: regression, classification, regularisation, model selection, clustering, and evaluation. Students implement core algorithms from scratch.

title: Software Engineering
description: Requirements engineering, software architecture, testing strategies, version control workflows, code review, and agile delivery. Teams build and ship a semester-long project.

title: Computer Graphics
description: Rasterisation, geometric transformations, shading models, texture mapping, ray tracing, and an introduction to GPU programming.

title: Advanced Machine Learning
description: Advanced topics in representation learning, optimisation for deep models, transfer learning, and model deployment. Requires a substantial research-style project.

title: Distributed Systems
description: Replication, consistency models, consensus, fault tolerance, and distributed storage. Readings from primary literature plus a systems project.

title: Natural Language Processing
description: Text representation, language models, sequence labelling, attention mechanisms, evaluation, and responsible deployment of language technologies.

title: Computer Vision
description: Image formation, convolution, feature detection, camera models, stereo, and modern learned approaches to recognition and segmentation.

title: Deep Learning
description: Neural network architectures, backpropagation, regularisation, convolutional and sequence models, and practical training workflows.

title: Calculus I
description: Limits, continuity, derivatives, applications of differentiation, and an introduction to integration.

title: Calculus II
description: Techniques of integration, sequences and series, polar coordinates, and an introduction to differential equations.

title: Honors Calculus I
description: Rigorous treatment of single-variable calculus for students with strong preparation. Covers limits, continuity, differentiation, and integration with proofs.

title: Linear Algebra
description: Vector spaces, linear transformations, matrices, determinants, eigenvalues, eigenvectors, and applications to data analysis.

title: Differential Equations
description: First-order equations, linear systems, Laplace transforms, and numerical solution techniques with applications in engineering and physics.

title: Probability Theory
description: Probability spaces, random variables, distributions, expectation, independence, limit theorems, and Markov chains.

title: Numerical Methods
description: Floating-point arithmetic, root finding, interpolation, numerical integration, linear systems, and iterative methods. Includes programming assignments.

title: Statistical Methods
description: Descriptive statistics, sampling distributions, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, and simple linear regression.

title: Regression Analysis
description: Multiple linear regression, model diagnostics, variable selection, logistic regression, and reproducible data analysis workflows.

title: Mechanics and Motion
description: Kinematics, Newtonian dynamics, work and energy, momentum, rotational motion, and oscillations. Calculus-based with weekly laboratory.

title: Electricity and Magnetism
description: Electrostatics, circuits, magnetic fields, induction, and Maxwell's equations with weekly laboratory.

title: Principles of Economics
description: Microeconomic and macroeconomic fundamentals: markets, elasticity, market failure, national accounts, inflation, and monetary policy.

title: Intermediate Microeconomics
description: Consumer and producer theory, market structure, general equilibrium, and welfare analysis using calculus-based methods.

title: Econometrics
description: Multiple regression, causal inference, instrumental variables, panel data, and applied empirical work with statistical software.

title: Introduction to Logic
description: Propositional and predicate logic, truth tables, natural deduction, and formal analysis of arguments.

title: Ethics of Technology
description: Ethical frameworks applied to privacy, algorithmic bias, automation, and professional responsibility in computing.

title: Academic Writing
description: Close reading, argument construction, research methods, and revision. Required writing seminar for all first-year students.

title: Technical Writing
description: Audience analysis, documentation, proposals, and technical reports. Practice writing for engineering and software contexts.
